description:
`psycopg2-binary` is a legacy PostgreSQL driver with known packaging
fragility (ships pre-compiled C extensions in a binary wheel, no async
support, soft-deprecated in many CI environments). `psycopg3` (package:
`psycopg[binary]`) is the successor — async-compatible, PEP 249 v3 compliant,
and actively maintained.

Surfaced as a deferred item in the DONE file for `tighten-dependencies-phase-plan`
(completed 2026-04-15): "Migration off psycopg2-binary to psycopg3 — driver
modernization — out of scope for an *elimination* audit. File separately when
product is ready."

This is not an elimination audit item — it is a deliberate driver swap that
may require updating connection-string parameters, cursor usage, and any
code that imports psycopg2 directly. Scope must be confirmed before
committing to the swap.

anti_patterns.dont: mix psycopg2 and psycopg3 imports across modules
anti_patterns.why: pick one and complete the migration fully

anti_patterns.dont: use psycopg3 async API in the synchronous adapter path without a separate design decision

deferrals.reason: Async usage is additive and out of scope for the synchronous driver swap; file as a follow-on if async PostgreSQL connections are desired.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Async psycopg3 interface filed as optional follow-on 'if desired'; no evidence of demand or a concrete plan.
deferrals.summary: Migrate to psycopg3 async interface for concurrent query paths

preserves.behavior: All Redshift and PostgreSQL benchmark runs produce identical results before and after the swap
Connection factory interface remains unchanged for any callers outside benchbox/platforms/

prior_art.concept: benchbox/platforms/postgres*.py, benchbox/platforms/redshift*.py — likely primary psycopg2 consumers
tighten-dependencies-phase-plan DONE file — deferred this item explicitly

verifications.description: No psycopg2 imports remain after migration

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/ -k 'redshift or postgres' -q

work_units.notes:
grep -rn 'psycopg2\|import psycopg' benchbox/ tests/
Classify each site: direct import, connection factory, cursor type
assumption, exception type catch. Estimate the change surface.
Also check if any tests mock psycopg2 internals that would need updating.
work_units.summary: Audit all psycopg2 import sites and connection usage patterns

work_units.notes:
psycopg3 is largely API-compatible with psycopg2 for synchronous use, but
there are known differences: parameter placeholders (%s vs %(name)s vs ?),
copy API, server-side cursors, and exception hierarchy. For each call site
found in w0, note whether it works unchanged or needs updating.
work_units.summary: Assess psycopg3 API compatibility at each identified call site

work_units.notes:
In pyproject.toml, replace psycopg2-binary with psycopg[binary] (or
psycopg[c] for the C extension build). Update any `import psycopg2` to
`import psycopg`. Keep a compatibility shim if the change surface from w1
is large — prefer a single incremental swap over a big-bang refactor.
work_units.summary: Swap psycopg2-binary for psycopg[binary] in pyproject.toml and update imports

work_units.notes:
uv run -- python -m pytest tests/ -k 'redshift or postgres or postgresql' -q
Also run the full unit suite to catch any indirect psycopg2 dependency
via transitive imports. Fix any failures before marking this done.
work_units.summary: Run the full Redshift/PostgreSQL test suite and confirm zero regressions
